The tetrahedron can be placed with vertices  

\[
A=(-5,0,0),\;B=(5,0,0),\;C=(0,15,0),\;D=\Bigl(0,\frac{21}{5},\frac{72}{5}\Bigr).
\]

Here the edges \(AB=10,\;CD=18\) and the four lateral edges each have length \(5\sqrt{10}\).  

The line through the midpoints of \(AB\) and \(CD\) (the symmetry axis) is the \(y\!-\!z\) line through \((0,0,0)\) and \(\bigl(0,\frac{48}{5},\frac{36}{5}\bigr)\); its length is \(12\).

\[
S=\Bigl(0,\frac{20}{3},5\Bigr),\qquad 
OS=\frac{25}{3}.
\]

Hence the circumradius is \(R_{\text{circ}}=\frac{5\sqrt{34}}{3}\).

The incenter \(R\) also lies on the same axis. Using the plane equations of the faces and setting the distances from a point \((0,y,z)\) to the faces \(ABC\) and \(ACD\) equal gives

\[
y=\frac{15}{4},\qquad z=\frac{45}{16}.
\]

Thus  

\[
R=\Bigl(0,\frac{15}{4},\frac{45}{16}\Bigr),\qquad 
OR=\frac{75}{16}.
\]

The distance between the two centers is therefore  

\[
RS=OS-OR=\frac{25}{3}-\frac{75}{16}
      =\frac{175}{48}.
\]

Written as \(\frac{m}{n}\) with \(\gcd(m,n)=1\), we have \(m=175,\;n=48\).  
Hence \(m+n=175+48=223\).

\[
\boxed{223}
\]
